axis evidence is secondary (earnings-call transcripts, trade press, company revenue releases), not primary filings

cluster_thesis.text: AI wafer and packaging capex is still accelerating -- WFE consensus roughly +30% YoY into 2027 and TSMC CoWoS capacity targeted to roughly double from 130-140k wpm in Q4 2026 to 190-200k by end-2027. But leadership inside the cluster has rotated from wafer starts to the steps whose share of each capex dollar is rising: advanced packaging, test, and process control. Front-end wafer capacity is no longer where the incremental dollar earns the most.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: TSMC monthly revenue printing below +25% YoY for two consecutive months, or any cut to the 190-200k wpm end-2027 CoWoS capacity path disclosed on or before the 2026-10-15 Q3 call.

margin_pool.moving_toward: Advanced packaging (CoWoS/OSAT), test, and process control/metrology -- process steps whose share of each capex dollar is rising as gate-all-around and 2.5D/3D packaging ramp.
margin_pool.moving_away_from: Mature-node front-end wafer capacity and China-exposed DUV lithography, where policy risk and domestic substitution cap the profit pool even as unit shipments grow.

evidence.claim: Test equipment has risen from 7% to 8% of total semicap spend in 2026
evidence.source: Teradyne CEO, Q2 FY2026 earnings call transcript

evidence.claim: TSMC CoWoS capacity target raised to 130-140k wafers/month for Q4 2026, with 190-200k/month targeted by end-2027; ASE ramping from ~20k to 40-45k over the same window
WFE spending expected to grow 30%+ YoY in 2027 -- the front end catches up, but off a base where test and packaging led
China will contribute ~20% of ASML 2026 net sales, and the MATCH Act under Congressional review would bar DUV exports to China outright
evidence.source: CNBC, US-China AI feud / ASML export coverage

differentiator_reads.axis: share of WFE spend captured, and whether it is rising
differentiator_reads.read: Test has gone from 7% to 8% of semicap spend in 2026 -- the only sourced rising-share figure in this cluster. Price leadership (+8.80pp rel_intra) is therefore corroborated by a fundamental share gain, not coincidence.
differentiator_reads.source: Teradyne Q2 FY2026 earnings call transcript

differentiator_reads.axis: process-step mix -- which steps gain intensity as GAA and advanced packaging ramp
differentiator_reads.read: Test intensity rises with die complexity and with known-good-die requirements in 2.5D packaging, the fastest-growing step in the chain.

ranking.case_against: Over the ATR risk cap (headroom -$94, cap_multiple 1.056) so the book cannot add. RSI 48.1 says the +8.28% one-month move is already stale. And Teradyne itself guides 2027 only as 'healthy growth' while WFE is guided +30% -- the front end out-grows test next year, which would reverse this rank.

differentiator_reads.axis: process-step mix -- which steps gain intensity as GAA and advanced packaging ramp
differentiator_reads.read: Process control and metrology intensity rises fastest at gate-all-around and in advanced packaging: more layers and more inspection steps per wafer, so KLA's dollars-per-wafer rise faster than wafer starts. This is the rank most at odds with the cache, which has no return for KLAC at all.
differentiator_reads.source: KLA Q4 FY2026 earnings call read-through

differentiator_reads.read: Q4 FY26 revenue $3.66B and non-GAAP EPS $1.05 at or above the high end of guidance, with a $7B buyback and an accelerating 2026-2027 outlook -- spend share defended and growing across leading-edge logic, HBM, and advanced packaging.
differentiator_reads.source: state.thesis KLAC evidence_for; KLA Q4 FY26 print

ranking.case_against: The stock fell ~9.6% on that beat -- an expectations reset that is explicitly unresolved and can recur at the next print. RSI 37.2 says the market has not re-rated it, and I have no cached return to test whether the reset is still working through. Ranking a name second on fundamentals when the cache cannot see its price is the weakest link in this ladder.

differentiator_reads.axis: advanced packaging (CoWoS-class) capacity as a bottleneck distinct from wafer capacity
differentiator_reads.read: TSM owns the scarcest asset in the chain and sets its price. CoWoS target raised to 130-140k wpm for Q4 2026 and 190-200k by end-2027 -- ranked above NVDA against the price ordering because the capacity owner, not the capacity consumer, captures the scarcity rent.
July 2026 revenue NT$467.58bn, +44.7% YoY and +5.6% MoM -- growth overwhelmingly leading-edge, with minimal mature-node overcapacity drag.

ranking.case_against: Single-geography concentration risk that no other cluster member carries at this magnitude. And the CoWoS ramp itself erodes the scarcity rent that justifies this rank -- doubling capacity by end-2027 is exactly how a bottleneck stops being one.

differentiator_reads.axis: advanced packaging (CoWoS-class) capacity as a bottleneck distinct from wafer capacity
differentiator_reads.read: NVDA is the demand node, not a share-of-spend node -- its output is gated by CoWoS and HBM, both of which it buys rather than owns. Ranked below TSM despite a higher rel_intra_pp (+8.65pp) for exactly this reason.
differentiator_reads.source: SemiWiki CoWoS capacity tracking; fusionww AI-bottleneck analysis

differentiator_reads.axis: foundry/IDM customer concentration and whether the customer is itself gaining share
differentiator_reads.read: NVDA is TSMC's most important leading-edge and packaging customer and is still gaining accelerator share, which is what keeps it in the top half.

ranking.case_against: RSI 70.4 -- by far the most crowded name in the cluster, and the only one where price alone would flag extension. The OpenAI/SB Energy arrangement (guarantee narrowed from $250bn to ~$100bn first phase, ~$3bn direct stake unsigned) is vendor-financed demand, lower-quality than organic order flow.

differentiator_reads.axis: process-step mix -- litho vs depo vs etch vs metrology vs test
differentiator_reads.read: Etch and deposition step counts rise materially with gate-all-around and 3D DRAM architectures, so LRCX's served-step intensity grows faster than wafer starts. Record Q4 revenue $6.72bn with raised guidance corroborates.

ranking.case_against: The most DRAM-capex-levered name in the cluster, so it inherits any memory pricing peak directly -- and memory contract pricing is the part of the AI-capex complex closest to late-cycle. rel_smh_pp of +12.6 also suggests a good deal of the re-rating has happened.

differentiator_reads.axis: process-step mix -- which steps gain intensity as GAA and advanced packaging ramp
differentiator_reads.read: Deposition, etch and CVD step counts rise with gate-all-around and packaging; AMAT serves the broadest step set in the cluster and carries no single-policy kill switch. Ranked ABOVE ASML against the price ordering (-2.85pp vs +1.31pp) on this basis.
differentiator_reads.source: The Diligence Stack WFE outlook; Deloitte 2026 semiconductor outlook

differentiator_reads.axis: leading-edge vs mature-node revenue split, and exposure to mature-node overcapacity
differentiator_reads.read: AMAT carries the largest mature-node and China mix of the WFE trio, the offsetting drag on this rank -- though 2026 evidence is that mature-node shortage and overcapacity coexist, with AI-driven power-management demand tightening 8-inch supply.
differentiator_reads.source: CSIS mature-node overcapacity analysis; SCMP coverage

ranking.case_against: RSI 33.3 and a negative rel_intra_pp -- the market is voting the other way and has been for a month. If the mature-node/China mix is the reason, my rank is simply wrong and the price is right. The falsifier is AMAT's October print: China revenue mix rising rather than falling.

differentiator_reads.axis: China export-control exposure: revenue at risk, licences held, and domestic substitution
differentiator_reads.read: China is ~20% of 2026 net sales and the MATCH Act under Congressional review would bar DUV exports to China outright. This is the axis that decides the rank -- a policy kill switch no other cluster member carries.
differentiator_reads.source: CNBC, US-China AI feud / ASML export coverage

differentiator_reads.axis: share of WFE spend captured, and whether it is rising or defended
differentiator_reads.read: ASML has stopped publishing quarterly bookings -- removing the single best forward WFE indicator this cluster had, which degrades the whole cluster's visibility, not just ASML's.

ranking.case_against: Q2 2026 bookings came in at EUR5.5bn against EUR4.8bn consensus -- a clear beat. The EUV monopoly is untouched by China's DUV progress (5 units in 2026 vs ASML's 131 immersion tools, 98.7% share), so this rank penalises a policy risk that may never crystallise.

differentiator_reads.axis: foundry/IDM customer concentration and whether the customer is itself gaining share
differentiator_reads.read: AMD is gaining accelerator and server share as a TSMC customer -- Q2 revenue $11.54bn beat with Data Center revenue +107% YoY. Ranked ABOVE the price-laggard slot (-10.03pp rel_intra) because share gain at the customer level is a real cluster axis and INTC has no equivalent.

differentiator_reads.axis: advanced packaging capacity as a distinct bottleneck
differentiator_reads.read: AMD holds no owned capacity, process-step, or packaging position -- it competes for the same CoWoS allocation NVDA does, from a weaker priority position. That is what caps it at 8 rather than higher.

ranking.case_against: Q3 guidance read as below consensus (2026-08-11) and the ~$5bn investment-grade debt raise (2026-08-14) levers the balance sheet to fund capex it does not own. The one-month price is the worst in the cluster by a wide margin and I am explicitly overriding it -- if the guide-down is the start of a share-loss trend rather than a one-quarter reset, price is right and I am wrong.

differentiator_reads.axis: foundry/IDM customer concentration and whether the customer is itself gaining share
differentiator_reads.read: The only cluster member that is a net CONSUMER of WFE while running negative economics: trailing EPS -$2.09 and profit margin -19.8%. An IDM whose own capex is the swing factor sits at the wrong end of a rising-capex cluster.

IFS foundry external wins remain thin (Fortinet named); leading-edge external foundry revenue is not yet a material share, so INTC captures the AI tailwind mainly through CPU pricing rather than through capacity or process-step position.

ranking.case_against: Q2 revenue +25% YoY with server and laptop CPU price hikes on AI demand, a $5.7bn Leixlip AI-capacity expansion, and a SoftBank stake -- the pivot has real funding and real early wins. It is also a brand-new position (5sh, 2026-08-07) with a thin track record, so the laggard call rests on economics rather than on observed execution failure.

differentiator_reads.axis: process-step mix and advanced packaging position
differentiator_reads.read: QCOM has no fab, no WFE, and no packaging-capacity position -- it does not express any of this cluster's differentiator axes. Ranked last on relevance to the cluster question, not on company conviction.

ranking.case_against: Position is $0.13 -- a dust remnant at 0.000% weight. This rank is administrative and carries no rotation information; QCOM is not a usable funding source and should not be read as one.

redundant_pairs.same_bet_because: Not one bet -- they are vendor and customer. ASML sells EUV/DUV tools TO TSM. Their dominant risks are opposed, not shared: ASML's is US/NL export policy (MATCH Act, ~20% China sales), TSM's is geographic concentration and packaging pricing power. A MATCH Act passage is a direct ASML negative and neutral-to-mildly-positive for TSM. The near-identical one-month move (0.63pp gap) and volatility (0.47pp) is coincidence of a shared tailwind, exactly what the screen warns about.

Literally opposite sides of the same transaction -- AMAT sells wafer fab equipment, INTC buys it. An INTC capex cut is an AMAT revenue negative. They also sit on opposite sides of every differentiator axis. Consolidating them would remove a real hedge, not a duplicate.

bench.entry_condition: On confirmation that OSAT CoWoS capacity is ramping to the 40-45k wpm end-2027 path, or on a pullback below $44. AMKR is a pure OSAT advanced-packaging play -- the exact axis the margin pool is migrating toward and the one axis this book has no direct expression of.

Pullback to ~$240, or a disclosed packaging-inspection order/backlog step-up at the next print. ONTO is packaging-specific metrology and inspection, so its step intensity rises faster than AMAT's broad depo/etch set with far less mature-node and China mix.
Below $235. MKSI supplies subsystems and lasers levered to advanced packaging and litho without ASML's single-policy China kill switch.
Below $130. Smallest and most levered pure packaging-inspection expression; higher beta to the same margin-pool migration.

thesis_tensions.tension: No tension in direction, but a tension in evidence base: state.thesis rates KLAC strengthening and I rank it 2, yet the compute cache has NO one-month return for it. Two agents agreeing on a name neither has priced this run, and RSI 37.2 is the one observable that dissents from both.

state.thesis has AMAT strengthening and I rank it above ASML on step-intensity, yet AMAT's rel_intra_pp is -2.85 with RSI 33.3. The ladder and the thesis agree with each other and both disagree with price. That is a shared exposure to being wrong, not independent confirmation.

Direct tension with the live cluster_rotation pair P-237/P-238 (Sell AMD -> Buy NVDA), built on the SMH-relative reading. On cluster-internal fundamental axes AMD is rank 8, not the laggard -- INTC is. state.thesis's watch status is consistent with rank 8, but the proposal treats AMD as the funding source, and this ladder does not support that selection.
No tension -- watch status and the laggard call agree. Flagged only so the merge sees that the laggard designation moved from AMD (price) to INTC (fundamentals).
Not a real disagreement: my rank measures relevance to the semis/fabs capex axes, on which QCOM scores zero, and the position is $0.13 of dust. Do not read rank 10 as a thesis downgrade.
